profile.name: maxmya
profile.bio: I make small, sharp tools for the desktop and the terminal. This is the bench: what I'm building, what shipped, and the notes I didn't want to lose.

projects.name: AppShelf
projects.tagline: A shelf for every app on your Linux desktop.
projects.description: A keyboard-first application launcher and updater for Omarchy and Quickshell. AppShelf inventories what's installed, keeps it current, and updates itself from the same running AppImage it uses for everything else.

landing.headline:
EVERY APP.
ONE SHELF.
landing.deck: One place to see what's installed, what's stale, and what to launch next. No daemon farm, no cloud account, no telemetry.

blocks.title: WHAT IT DOES
items: Indexes installed applications and their current versions
One keystroke to update an app, one to update AppShelf itself
AppImage first, with a PKGBUILD in the source tree for Arch users
Lives alongside Quickshell instead of replacing your desktop

versions.title: Self-update lands
versions.notes: --self-check-update and --self-update now work on the running AppImage, the same way AppShelf updates every application it manages.

versions.title: Same-day follow-up
versions.notes: Tightened the self-update path and fixed AppImage detection edge cases.

versions.title: Install flow reworked
versions.notes: Simplified install and integration flags, with clearer Omarchy requirements.

updates.title: AppShelf can now update itself
updates.body: The updater that powers every managed app now works on AppShelf itself. Same flags, same flow, no separate bootstrap script.

projects.name: tokmon
projects.tagline: A small meter for a big number.
projects.description: A terminal-native token monitor. It keeps an eye on what your workflows are spending and prints the answer without a dashboard, a browser tab, or an account.

landing.headline:
KNOW WHAT
IT COSTS.
landing.deck: Token accounting for people who live in a terminal. Plain text out, easy to pipe, easy to script.

blocks.title: DESIGN NOTES
items: Readable output that plays nicely with grep and friends
No network calls, no telemetry, no hidden state
Fits in a status bar or a shell prompt
MIT licensed and small enough to audit in one sitting

updates.title: tokmon moved to a cleaner output format
updates.body: Dropped the decorative framing. What's left is a line of text you can actually pipe into something else.

projects.name: Droneia
projects.tagline: Backend services for things that fly.
projects.description: The Java service layer behind the Droneia project: ingestion, state and the boring reliability work that keeps a fleet of experiments from stepping on each other.

landing.headline:
STEADY HANDS
ON THE WIRES.
landing.deck: A service layer built for telemetry that arrives out of order and clients that reconnect at the worst possible moment.

blocks.title: SCOPE
items: Clear boundaries between transport, domain and storage
Shared contracts for the Kotlin and TypeScript front ends

projects.name: Droneia Frontend
projects.description: Web front end for Droneia. Turns the service layer's state into something a human can read at a glance.

landing.headline:
A VIEW OF
THE FLIGHT.
landing.deck: Built against the Droneia service contracts, with an eye for dense information that stays legible.

projects.name: DroneiaK
projects.description: Kotlin take on the Droneia client. Reactive streams, explicit state, and the same service contracts as the other front ends.

landing.headline:
ANOTHER WAY
TO LISTEN.
landing.deck: A second client for the same backend, built to see how far a reactive model carries before it gets in the way.

projects.name: dotfiles
projects.description: My Linux and terminal setup: Lua, shell, and the small alignments that make a workspace feel like a workspace. Rebuilt more often than it should be.

landing.headline:
THE MACHINE,
WRITTEN DOWN.
landing.deck: A living record of keys, colors and small conveniences. Clone it, steal the parts that make sense, leave the rest.

projects.name: Zamboka Version
projects.tagline: A version check with a pulse.
projects.description: Godot-side version handling for the Zamboka experiments: compare, report and fail loudly when a build and its content disagree.

landing.headline:
BUILD VS
CONTENT.
landing.deck: A tiny guard rail for Godot projects, so a build never quietly runs against the wrong version of its own data.

updates.title: The bench is open
updates.body: New home for the build log. Project pages, version history and wiki links now live in one place instead of scattered across README files.

updates.title: AppShelf 0.7.0
updates.body: Self-update shipped. The same update machinery used for managed apps now runs on the AppImage that's currently executing.

updates.title: Notes on agent constitutions
updates.body: A written constitution for AI agents went up as a separate repository. It's a document, not a framework, and that's deliberate.

updates.title: tokmon output, simplified
updates.body: Removed decoration from the CLI output. Pipeable text is the whole interface now.
